Stall speed increases, not decreases, when load factor is above 1.
Wingtip vortices are not laminar flow; they are rotating flow from pressure leakage.
Profile drag comprises form and skin-friction effects, not tip-vortex effects.
Pressure equalisation around the tips creates vortices and induced drag.
The vortices are a drag consequence of lift, not the source of lift itself.
51-097.note: Pressure leaks around the tips → vortices → induced drag.

why: The spiral dive description is right, but a spin typically has the inner wing more stalled in a turn.
A spin has a stalled inner wing and relatively low/steady airspeed; a spiral dive has unstalled wings and rapidly increasing speed.
This reverses the spin’s stall location and assigns the rapid speed increase to the spin instead of spiral dive.
A spin is not defined by rapidly increasing speed, and the spiral dive is not a constant-speed stalled state.
51-098.note: Spin = stalled autorotation; spiral dive = unstalled, steepening turn with rising speed.
